rationale: INCOMING_PY (ontology workstream), and the lane's own subject. Python resolves a callee at RUNTIME through the receiver's type and the MRO, so a method resolved at runtime has no static target — and this lane's job is to MEASURE that and report it rather than guess a target. The lane was already emitting the honest NAME (PY-11: dropping an uppercase callee lost 889 of 1,152 corpus edges, 77.2% of them for classes the file explicitly imports), but it emitted the name with nothing distinguishing the situations that produce it, and M14 §4 requires every edge below 1.0 to carry a machine-readable reason code. Measured over the 679-file INCOMING_PY corpus before this change: 29,877 `calls` edges at 0.9, 0 with a reason code; 14,580 `uses` at 0.9, 0; 1,454 `instantiates` at 0.9, 0; 1,498 `references` at 0.95, 0; and 81 of 670 `overrides` below 1.0 with none. All five labels are pinned here, and the dispatch partition they express is the corpus measurement: 6,422 in-file-symbol / 3,312 dispatch-on-parameter / 73 dispatch-on-receiver / 873 dispatch-through-alias / 16,549 external-member / 2,648 bare-global over 29,877 `calls` edges, i.e. 4,258 (14.3%) with no statically-nameable target. Nothing is DROPPED — the name is what the source wrote, and dropping it loses the fact — so the honesty is in the field, and this fixture is what stops the three dispatch classes from being silently collapsed back into one.

the receiver is a LOCAL, and its type is written down nowhere — `Store` is assigned to it in the same statement, which is an inference this lane does not make

NOT the same fact as the row above. `os` is a module root this file imported, so `os.path.join` is reachable through the import edge; collapsing it into dispatch-on-receiver would teach a consumer to discard an edge it can follow.

forbidSymbols.name: render
forbidSymbols.note: a method the runtime dispatches to but this file never declares is NOT a symbol. Publishing one would invent a definition; the `calls` edge carries the call site and `reasonCode: dispatch-on-parameter` carries the uncertainty.

_seamNote.what: `reasonCode` on every relationship the lane emits below confidence 1.0, and `qualified` on the member-read and dispatch edges. `qualified` is the spelling the source wrote (`self.store.save`, `os.path.join`) and `target` is the leaf it names.
_seamNote.why: M14 §4 asks for a machine-readable reason code rather than a number because the number cannot be acted on. 0.9 on a `self.m()` and 0.9 on `os.path.join` mean opposite things — one has no reachable target and the other has one — and a consumer that had to infer which is which would have to re-derive the import vocabulary of every file. Putting the distinction on the edge makes 'how much of this graph is guesswork' (the §4 third clause) a SQL query: `SELECT reason_code, count(*) FROM relationships WHERE language='python' GROUP BY 1`.
_seamNote.notDropped: The edge is emitted in every dispatch case. PY-11 measured that dropping an unresolvable callee loses the fact rather than qualifying it, and that measurement has not been contradicted. What this change does is stop the lane from asserting a target it cannot justify WITHOUT SAYING SO.
